title: SA JWTs are minted but never validated on inbound requests
description: auth.rs:83-111 authenticate() only checks the static bearer token file. SA JWTs minted by handlers/tokens.rs are never verified on inbound requests — a request with a valid SA JWT header is authenticated as system:anonymous. Fix: add JWT verification path in authenticate(). Load the RSA public key from --sa-pub at startup. On a Bearer token that fails static map lookup, attempt RS256 JWT decode and verify. On success, extract sub (system:serviceaccount:ns:name) as username and construct groups [system:serviceaccounts, system:serviceaccounts:ns]. On failure, return BadToken. The encoding key is already loaded at startup (main.rs:82-96); load the corresponding DecodingKey from sa.pub.

title: RBAC index not updated when roles/bindings are written via API
description: The generic handler (generic.rs) writes RBAC objects (ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings, Roles, RoleBindings) to the store but never calls rbac_index.apply_object() or rbac_index.remove_object(). Creating or deleting a ClusterRole via kubectl has no effect on the in-memory RBAC index — policy enforcement is stale until restart (and restart doesn't help either, see mayor-vgr). Fix: after each successful put/delete in the generic handler, check if the key is under /apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/ and call apply_object/remove_object accordingly. Depends on: mayor-vgr (startup scan) — both must land together for RBAC to work end-to-end.

title: RBAC index not populated from store on startup — restarts open the cluster
description: state.rs:18-27 creates a fresh empty RbacIndex on every startup. rbac.rs:82-113 has apply_object() and remove_object() but they are never called. Effect: any RBAC roles and bindings stored on a previous run are invisible after restart — every restart produces an open cluster with no policy. Fix: in AppState::new() (or main.rs boot sequence), list the /apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/ prefix from the store and call rbac_index.apply_object() for each item. This must run before the server starts accepting requests.

title: Watch not implemented for generic resources (Deployments, ConfigMaps, Secrets, RBAC, etc.)
description: generic.rs:61-66 — check_watch() returns 400 for ALL watch requests on non-Pod resources. kubectl informers and Argo CD watch Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and RBAC objects constantly. Without this, any kubectl --watch or controller using informers will fail immediately. The store already supports watch() — this is purely a handler gap. Fix: implement a generic watch response path in list_resource and list_namespaced_resource, similar to watch_pods in handlers/pods.rs. Emit NDJSON with ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED/BOOKMARK events and a 60s bookmark timer.

title: Worker agents don't inherit settings.local.json permissions
description: Background agents dispatched via the Agent tool run with a clean permission set and do not inherit the project's .claude/settings.local.json allowlist. This causes agents to get permission-blocked on basic operations (bd *, find, ls) and then the fewer-permission-prompts skill hijacks the session. Root cause: settings.local.json is scoped to the main session, not sub-agent sessions. Fix: move the allow list into settings.json (which may be inherited) or find another mechanism to propagate permissions to sub-agents. Observed in Phase 3 audit dispatch — two consecutive agents failed.
close_reason: worker agent config created at .claude/agents/worker.md with permissionMode: auto

title: Spec: State store — SQLite vs LMDB trade-off analysis and schema design
description: Produce a decision doc + spec for the u7s state store. Compare SQLite vs LMDB on: memory footprint, write throughput for typical K8s workloads, watch/notify support (K8s watch requires efficient resource version tracking), tooling ergonomics, Rust crate maturity. Make a recommendation. If SQLite: design the schema. If LMDB: design the key layout. Output: /ai/prompts/state-store.md
close_reason: State store spec written to /ai/prompts/state-store.md (932 lines). Recommendation: SQLite. Rationale: target workload peaks at ~17 writes/second; SQLite WAL handles >1000 writes/s with p99 <10ms — two orders of magnitude headroom. LMDB advantages irrelevant at this scale; lmdb-rkv crate is dormant; MDB_MAP_FULL is operational risk. Covers: K8s storage semantics, full SQLite spec with DDL+connection pool, full LMDB spec with DBI layout+heed, comparison table, benchmark spec with decision thresholds, Store trait implementation signatures for both, watch notification with subscribe-before-replay race-free pattern, phased delivery.

title: CRD support — required for Argo CD milestone
description: No CRD plumbing exists. Argo CD requires the following CRDs: Application, AppProject (argoproj.io/v1alpha1), plus Rollout, AnalysisTemplate, etc. for progressive delivery. CRD support requires: (1) CustomResourceDefinition storage and CRUD via generic handler, (2) dynamic routing — when a CRD is created, the API server must begin serving /apis/<group>/<version>/<plural> for custom resources, (3) discovery must advertise CRD-defined groups, (4) schema validation stub (can be permissive in Phase 3). This is the largest single Phase 3 work item.

title: namespaces resource missing from /api/v1 discovery resource list
description: types.rs:76-133 V1_RESOURCES does not include namespaces. kubectl get namespaces and any client that reads /api/v1 before listing namespaces will either get a 404 or silently skip namespace operations. The namespace handlers are fully implemented (handlers/namespaces.rs) — this is just a missing entry in the static discovery list. Fix: add a namespaces ApiResource entry to V1_RESOURCES with verbs [create, delete, get, list, patch, update, watch] and namespaced: false.

title: Scale subresource missing for Deployments, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets
description: Deployments, ReplicaSets, and StatefulSets are registered in state.rs:69-71 but have no /scale subresource handler. kubectl scale, kubectl rollout, and HPA all use GET/PATCH /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/:ns/deployments/:name/scale. The Scale object has spec.replicas; a PUT/PATCH writes spec.replicas back to the workload object. Fix: add scale subresource routes to main.rs and implement handlers that read/write spec.replicas on the stored object. Also add scale to the verbs list in apps_v1_resources() in discovery.rs.

title: authorization.k8s.io and authentication.k8s.io groups missing from /apis discovery
description: discovery.rs:23-32 api_group_list() advertises only apps and rbac.authorization.k8s.io. The authorization.k8s.io group (SSAR/SSRR endpoints) and authentication.k8s.io group (TokenRequest) are wired and functional but not advertised. Well-behaved clients discover available groups from /apis before calling endpoints — missing entries cause some clients to skip these APIs entirely. Fix: add authorization.k8s.io/v1 and authentication.k8s.io/v1 to api_group_list(), and add corresponding api_group_resources() cases with their resource lists (selfsubjectaccessreviews, selfsubjectrulesreviews, tokenreviews).

title: Cross-namespace pod list (GET /api/v1/pods) returns 404
description: main.rs:157-171 registers /api/v1/:resource for generic cluster-scoped resources. A GET /api/v1/pods hits core_list_resource which calls list_resource with plural=pods. pods is not in the resource registry (state.rs:55-80) as a cluster-scoped resource — only as namespaced. Result: 404. kubectl get pods --all-namespaces (and equivalently kubectl get pods -A) uses this path. Argo CD uses it for drift detection. Fix: either (a) register pods as a cluster-scoped list-only resource in the registry and implement cross-namespace list by scanning /registry/pods/ prefix, or (b) special-case /api/v1/pods in the router to scan all namespaces.

title: watch verb missing from all discovery resource lists
description: types.rs:69 CORE_VERBS = [create, delete, get, list, patch, update] — watch is absent. discovery.rs:82-148 apps/v1 and rbac resource lists also omit watch. kubectl --watch and informer-based clients (Argo CD, kube-controller-manager) check the verbs list before issuing watch requests; some clients refuse watch when the verb is absent. Fix: add watch to CORE_VERBS and to all resource verb arrays in discovery.rs. This is a trivial one-liner but blocks watch adoption by well-behaved clients.

title: Discovery serverAddress hardcoded to 127.0.0.1:6443 — breaks remote kubectl
description: types.rs:28-33 SERVER_ADDRESS_BY_CLIENT_CIDRS hardcodes https://127.0.0.1:6443. kubectl on a remote machine receives the wrong server address from /api discovery and may redirect requests to the wrong host. Fix: derive the advertised address from the --listen flag, or add an --advertise-address CLI argument. Inject it into AppState and pass it through to the APIVersions struct (currently a static). This is a conformance issue: kube-bench checks that the advertised address is reachable.

title: Replace serde_json::Value with typed API models + Into/From conversions
description: discovery.rs and other handlers use json!() macros and serde_json::Value directly instead of typed structs. Define proper API representation types (e.g. ApiResourceList, ApiGroupList) with serde Serialize/Deserialize, and implement Into/From between internal models and API representations. This makes API versioning trivial — just add a v2 representation type — and makes the code self-documenting. Touches: crates/apiserver/src/types.rs, handlers/discovery.rs, and any other handler using raw Value.
design: Use Into/From traits between internal models and API representation types. Each API version gets its own representation module. Handlers work with internal types; serialisation boundary is at the response layer via Into. This is the canonical pattern for supporting v1/v2 API versioning without duplicating handler logic.
close_reason: Typed API models + Into/From merged — PR https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/3

Top risk: pod allocation accounting on MODIFIED/terminal events — requires pod_allocations side-map keyed by UID.

title: Controller manager SA token provisioning — Phase 3 deferred item DB-05
description: DB-05 deferred: the controller manager currently uses system:masters admin client cert. Real SA token provisioning requires the controller manager to: (1) watch ServiceAccount objects, (2) call POST /api/v1/namespaces/:ns/serviceaccounts/:name/token (already implemented), (3) store the resulting token in a Secret, (4) mount the Secret into pods via the admission webhook or downward API. SA JWT validation must also be wired (mayor-n9a). This is a multi-step feature; the token minting endpoint exists — the gap is the controller loop and secret injection.

title: Scaffold crates/scheduler — Phase 3 deferred item DB-04
description: DB-04 deferred: crates/scheduler does not exist. An external kube-scheduler binary is acceptable for Phase 3 compatibility testing (it uses pods/binding which is implemented). But the Phase 3 goal is to scaffold the crate: (1) add crates/scheduler to Cargo workspace, (2) minimal binary that connects to the API server, watches unscheduled pods (spec.nodeName == ''), and calls pods/binding with a simple scheduling decision (first available node). This unblocks end-to-end pod scheduling without depending on upstream kube-scheduler.

title: Add max watch duration — stuck clients hold streams forever
description: handlers/pods.rs:166-251 watch_pods stream has no timeout or max-duration enforcement. The Kubernetes spec requires servers to terminate watch streams after a server-defined max duration (typically 5-10 minutes) and send a BOOKMARK before closing. A stuck or abandoned client currently holds the stream open indefinitely. Fix: add a max watch duration (configurable, default 5 minutes) using tokio::time::sleep or interval. On expiry, emit a final BOOKMARK with the last_rv and close the stream gracefully. Apply the same pattern when generic watch is implemented (mayor-4z5).

title: Remove dead key_prefix() stub from store
description: store/src/lib.rs:497-504 key_prefix() returns key.to_string() — a no-op. The comment says it stores the prefix on InternalEvent but push_event callers in put() and delete() (lines 533, 552) pass the full key as the prefix field, and watch() filters using event.key.starts_with(&prefix_owned) not event.prefix. The prefix field on InternalEvent is never read by the watch filter. Fix: remove key_prefix(), inline the key string directly in the push_event calls. Optionally remove the unused prefix field from InternalEvent entirely.

title: pods.rs duplicates resource version parsing instead of using generic.rs helper
description: generic.rs:110-119 has parse_resource_version() as a shared helper. handlers/pods.rs:324-333 and pods.rs:375-381 and pods.rs:466-475 have inline copies of the same match block. Fix: import and use parse_resource_version() from generic.rs (or move it to a shared module). Low risk — identical logic, pure cleanup.

title: Deduplicate RFC3339 time formatting — same algorithm copied 3 times
description: The Gregorian calendar to RFC3339 algorithm is copy-pasted verbatim in: generic.rs:178-225 (utc_now_rfc3339 + days_to_ymd), handlers/pods.rs:490-523 (utc_now_rfc3339), handlers/tokens.rs:174-201 (secs_to_rfc3339). These are identical modulo variable names. Fix: extract to a shared module (e.g. crate::time with utc_now_rfc3339() and secs_to_rfc3339(secs: u64)) and replace all three call sites. Remove days_to_ymd from generic.rs (it is only called internally). Low risk — pure refactor with no behavior change.
